workload.built_with: RUSTFLAGS=-C force-frame-pointers=yes supplied by the gateway, not by the project

phases.delta_from_quality: exactly one appended rule group allowing perf_event_open

cases.note: zero samples is a declared result, not an error
errno 1 is EPERM: the syscall is refused by the profile itself

observations: All 16 online CPUs opened, mapped and armed an inherited event; the kernel refuses to mmap the ring of an inherited event opened with cpu == -1, which is why the helper fans out per CPU.
Symbols are emitted in their raw v0 mangled form. The product does not demangle and does not claim to.
198 of 2154 frames did not resolve and are counted as such; they are not hidden.
No emitted frame contains a '/', so no module path reached the artifact.
limitations: Qualified on the Linux ARM64 guest only. Mach-O and PE are not qualified by this positive.
Frame-pointer unwinding only: a binary built without frame pointers yields shorter stacks, which the counters declare.
Effective depth is additionally capped by the kernel's perf_event_max_stack (127 by default).
provenance: MANUAL SMOKE, not a product-path receipt. These cases were run by hand with docker directly, before the gateway existed, to decide ADR-074. They are evidence that the containment works; they are NOT the qualification of rust.profile.flamegraph.
qualification_receipt: docs/validation/M5-03-runtime.json is the reproducible receipt written by the native test itself; prefer it.
known_divergences_from_the_product_path: The zero-sample case passes `--zero` on the child's argv. The product passes the profiled child no argument at all, so this exact invocation is unreachable through the gateway; the native test uses a separate zero-sample binary target instead.
The positive counters here (195 samples, 2154 frames, 198 unresolved) differ from the reproducible receipt's, because they are a different run on a different day.
The denial case here has no corresponding selection in the generated receipt. Treat the denial oracle as pending until it appears in M5-03-runtime.json.
